clue.text: Author shows little bird dissecting string

explanation.surface: A writer reveals a small bird slicing through a piece of string.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits inside the string: LA-WREN-CE, the novelist D. H. Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence was an English novelist and poet, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Counterfoil reveals rise in objections

explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the Scottish word for a girl, as well as the name of the film collie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is a Scots and northern English term for a young woman or female child.

clue.text: Postponed a song in action

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a fax as just one example of something that sends.

taken as written

clue.text: Eager to get some boned geese

clue.text: Patient is sadly not alert

clue.text: Joint of meat given to friend properly

clue.text: Bright sun due to revolve

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Male flirt to turn up and gush

the last letter of love
